analysis.title: Washington Matters: Post-Midterm Takeaways Across Markets
key_insights: Democrats won larger majorities than expected: 5-6 Senate seats and 37 or more House seats. They also flipped governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas. The Senate majority is not veto-proof, so federal gridlock is expected.
Democratic wins in key data-center states raise the risk of tighter local regulation of data centers. BofA expects this to slow, not derail, the AI investment boom.

Congress has 19 days left in session. It must pass an FY2027 budget or a continuing resolution before the current CR expires on December 11. It also needs to pass the NDAA. Republicans may try to address the debt ceiling before Democrats take control, and permitting reform could advance.

BofA expects the US debt limit to bind in February 2027 (previously May). Extraordinary measures should let Treasury keep paying until a November 2027 X-date. The Treasury General Account will be uncomfortably low in August.

Rates: the election is a headwind to BofA's pay-front-end and curve-flattening bias. BofA keeps both views given resilient growth, sticky inflation, a healthy labor market and resilient consumer spending.

USD: oil and US-tech declines would normally weigh on the dollar, and equities and commodities reacted that way after the election, but the USD appreciated. BofA cites continued US data outperformance and relative central bank repricing, and sees the fundamental backdrop staying positive for the USD into 2027.

Oil scenarios for Brent: a ceasefire in US-Iran, Saudi-Houthi or Russia-Ukraine conflicts could push it toward $80/bbl or lower next year. A 'neither war nor peace' outcome keeps it near $100/bbl. A renewed US-Iran conflict could push it toward $150/bbl in 2027. BofA says the midterm result may not change Iran policy since Trump controls it.

Credit: divided government should limit major fiscal and policy changes and support bonds and credit. Historically, split government has been associated with lower Treasury yields and tighter spreads, though budget and debt-ceiling fights could add volatility.

Munis: gridlock is positive for munis. Risk shifts to the state and local level, where tax constraints and data-center opposition could delay projects and pressure some local governments and utilities.

Equities strategy: BofA calls a Democratic sweep of Congress the least favorable scenario for equities and says a Republican president with a Democratic Congress has historically been the weakest backdrop for S&P 500 returns. A blue sweep was already priced by prediction markets and the Nasdaq fell 10% pre-election, so any further selloff should be temporary.
Utilities: Georgia is the clearest downside, since both executive and commission control changed. Failure to advance the permitting reform package would be negative for the sector.

Energy: behind-the-meter power buildout, especially in Texas, could slow. SMID-cap behind-the-meter stocks fell 13% the day after the election. BofA believes they were already pricing in no upside and sees upside as focus returns to core businesses. BofA's energy coverage fell 6% that day.
Industrials: if governors in TX, OH, GA and MI stop new development, about 60% of the US data center pipeline is unaffected, per Bloomberg. Limited new supply would benefit incumbents.

Homebuilders: a data center slowdown would be a net positive for housing stocks through lower rates and less competition for labor and materials. The ITB rose 7.3% versus the S&P 500's 1.6%, but BofA warns the 2027 new-construction setup is still challenging and valuations are ahead of fundamentals.

Tech hardware: the selloff came from lower multiples, not lower earnings estimates. BofA's FY28 EPS estimates are at or above consensus for most of the group. Even if US data center capacity additions fall 58% short of the bull case, FY28 EPS falls only 11-36% for most names.
Semis: BofA says indiscriminate selling of chip stocks on AI capex fears could run its course by early CY27, and data center policy clarity could drive a Q1 recovery.

Health care: Democrats are expected to vote to reverse Medicaid cuts and reinstate enhanced ACA subsidies, but major legislation is unlikely under Trump. BofA sees more multiple risk for hospitals and limited downside for managed care.

Defense: BofA's framework points to 7.6% annual real growth in defense modernization (procurement plus RDT&E) over FY2027-29e, as a larger House Democratic majority has historically supported higher modernization spending.

sector_views.rationale: A Democratic sweep is the least favorable scenario for equities, but further selling should be temporary because major policy change is hard to enact.
Georgia faces the clearest downside after executive and commission control changed. Failure to pass permitting reform would extend uncertainty.
The buildout could slow, but BofA sees upside in small and mid-cap names as focus returns to core businesses.
About 60% of the data center pipeline is unaffected by state opposition, and limited new supply would benefit incumbents.
A data center slowdown helps through lower rates and input costs, but the 2027 new-construction setup is challenging and valuations are stretched.
The selloff reflects lower multiples, not lower earnings, and FY28 EPS estimates remain at or above consensus.
Indiscriminate selling could run its course by early CY27, with a possible Q1 recovery on policy clarity and buybacks.
Estimates are unlikely to get a boost, so there is more multiple risk than upside.
Improving fundamentals should more than offset headline risk, with limited downside to the perceived losers.
A larger Democratic House majority has historically supported higher modernization spending.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Debt-limit negotiations are the key fiscal risk. Extraordinary measures should delay the X-date to November 2027.
Treasury can keep making payments until then, though the TGA will be uncomfortably low in August.
A ceasefire in the US-Iran, Saudi-Houthi or Russia-Ukraine conflicts could unlock supply and return the oil market to surplus.

macro_indicators.indicator: Brent crude ('neither war nor peace' scenario)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Constrained Iranian supply and persistent shipping risks keep the market tight.
With lower inventories, less responsive US shale and inelastic demand, a major disruption could push prices sharply higher.
Procurement plus RDT&E growth under BofA's political control framework.
Lower rates are a potential tailwind for housing.
Lower input costs could become a real tailwind for homebuilders.

crypto_views: BofA's brokers and exchanges analysts say the blue wave brings AI, crypto, prediction markets and taxes into focus, and that hearings will affect HOOD and COIN coverage.

risk_factors: Debt-limit negotiations are the key fiscal risk.
Budget and debt-ceiling brinkmanship could periodically add volatility to credit and rates.
Tighter state and local data center regulation, including possible construction pauses or moratoriums in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Michigan and New Mexico.
Failure to advance the permitting reform package would extend uncertainty for utilities and infrastructure.
A renewed US-Iran conflict could push Brent toward $150/bbl.
Higher regulation and taxes threaten future growth.
Moratorium threats could prompt developers and hyperscalers to accelerate projects, delaying cost relief for homebuilders.
vol_and_positioning: The Nasdaq shed 10% before the election, and BofA notes a blue sweep was already expected by prediction markets.
SMID-cap behind-the-meter energy stocks fell 13% the day after the election, and BofA believes they were already pricing in no upside.
AI-exposed IT hardware sold off on lower valuation multiples rather than lower earnings estimates.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: BofA says the midterm result may not change the situation since Trump controls policy. Stocks are pricing a higher chance of Trump ending the war, but the mechanism for peace is unclear.
A ceasefire in US-Iran, Saudi-Houthi and/or Russia-Ukraine conflicts could unlock energy supply and normalize trade routes.
A renewed US-Iran conflict is the key upside risk to oil.

tension_points.bull_case: A blue sweep was already priced in, with the Nasdaq down 10% pre-election. Major policy change is hard to enact, so any further selloff should be temporary. Tech hardware EPS is largely protected by contracts and diversified revenue.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA calls this the least favorable scenario for equities, with more policy uncertainty, risks to deregulation and risks to data centers. A Republican president with a Democratic Congress has historically been the weakest backdrop for S&P 500 returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Congressional failure to advance permitting reform, or campaign promises to pause data center construction being upheld by newly elected governors in Texas, Ohio, Georgia, Michigan and New Mexico.

tension_points.bull_case: Political opposition is a barrier to entry that benefits incumbents, and about 60% of the pipeline is unaffected. A slowdown helps homebuilders through lower rates and less competition for labor and materials.
tension_points.bear_case: Newly elected governors could stop construction in TX, OH, GA, MI and NM. Utilities, energy and industrial names tied to the buildout came under pressure, and behind-the-meter stocks fell 13%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Governors in TX, OH, GA and MI successfully stopping new development would test the 60% unaffected assumption.

theme_stances.key_argument: Democratic wins at federal and state levels increase policy uncertainty for utilities, energy and industrials tied to the data center buildout, though the AI investment boom should slow rather than derail.
theme_stances.evidence: increase policy uncertainty around data centers for utilities, energy, and industrial companies

theme_stances.key_argument: US data outperformance and relative central bank repricing outweigh midterm-related themes, keeping the fundamental backdrop positive for the USD into 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: we favored fading the conventional wisdom of USD depreciation

theme_stances.key_argument: Divided government limits major fiscal and policy changes, reducing uncertainty and supporting bonds and credit.
theme_stances.evidence: Gridlock should be positive for munis, reducing federal fiscal and tax-policy uncertainty
